taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station T-16 (survey area T). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 312.0 | 6.08 | 6.08
2 | 794.3 | 14.76 | 20.84
3 | 884.4 | 3.48 | 24.32
4 | 1280.2 | 10.95 | 35.27
5 | 4929.0 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as H-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Reference note: Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station: T-16
Curve type: A (letters AAA, since 312.0 < 794.3 < 884.4, 794.3 < 884.4 < 1280.2, and 884.4 < 1280.2 < 4929.0). Note: this does not match the on-file H-type classification — the resistivity sequence is monotonically increasing with depth, with no resistivity inversion, so the file label should be corrected to A-type.
Aquifer depth: 0 – 6.08 m (Layer 1, the lowest-resistivity unit, most consistent with a weathered/saturated zone; underlying layers increase steadily in resistivity, consistent with progressively more compact/resistive bedrock rather than a confined low-resistivity aquifer).
Recommendation: Target the 0–6.08 m weathered zone (Layer 1) as the primary water-bearing interval and set the first casing/screen interval there; flag the curve-type discrepancy (file says H, data indicates A) to the interpreting geophysicist before finalizing drill depth, and be prepared for reduced yield potential below ~6 m as resistivity rises toward compact bedrock.
